Research brief · As of 5 Oct 2026 (ET)

What is Merlin Labs?

A plain-language company definition for Merlin Labs / Merlin, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRLN): what Merlin Pilot is, how the company listed, where it sits in defense and civil aviation, and how the public parent relates to the operating company.

Independent · unaffiliated with Merlin IR Not investment advice

Company definition

Merlin, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRLN) builds Merlin Pilot, an aircraft-agnostic autonomy system meant to fly existing fixed-wing aircraft from takeoff to touchdown, with or without a human crew, for defense and civil use. The operating company is Merlin Labs, Inc.; the public parent is Merlin, Inc. after the March 2026 business combination. (company site · closing 8-K 20 Mar 2026)

Merlin Pilot

Merlin Pilot is the product claim behind both military airlift work (notably USSOCOM C-130J) and civil concepts (Condor cargo autonomy, SkyCourier UX with Textron). Company materials describe a single autonomy core across airframes rather than a one-off autopilot for a single type. (Merlin 24 Sep 2026 · May 13 prospectus)

Ticker and listing

Merlin listed through a SPAC merger with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. IV (formerly Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. I). The business combination agreement was signed 13 Aug 2025 at an $800M pre-money equity value. Shareholders voted on 12 Mar 2026; the deal closed 16 Mar 2026; Nasdaq trading as MRLN began 17 Mar 2026. (closing 8-K)

Business lines

  • Defense / government: More than 90% of revenue comes from U.S. government work, led by the USSOCOM C-130J sole-source IDIQ (ceiling $105M). Related work includes KC-135 progress with the Air Force and a GE Aerospace autonomy-core teaming. (Q2 10-Q · USAspending)
  • Civil certification: On 9 Sep 2026 Merlin said it is shutting down the small-aircraft New Zealand CAA certification program and concentrating civil certification investment on large aircraft, building on C-130J work. Kerikeri remains the flight-test center. (CEO note 9 Sep 2026)
  • OEM / concept partnerships: Includes Textron Aviation Cessna SkyCourier UX (14 Sep 2026), Northrop Grumman Beacon MOA, Honeywell Anthem MOU, Remah International (UAE), and Condor-related MOUs with World Star and IAI. (partnerships page)

Headquarters and facilities

  • Boston HQ — 100 Causeway, Floor 23, Boston, MA 02114 (lease commenced 23 Mar 2026; expires 31 Jan 2029). (Q2 10-Q)
  • Quonset State Airport, North Kingstown, RI — hangar and office; U.S. flight test moved here from Mojave in late 2024. (prospectus Facilities)
  • Kerikeri / Bay of Islands, NZ — dedicated flight-test and certification environment. (9 Sep note)
  • Hanscom Field / Bedford, MA — lease signed 4 Sep 2025; commencement expected in 2027. (10-Q)

Leadership snapshot

CEO / Chair Matthew George (founder; CEO since Nov 2018; combined Chair/CEO). Named public-company executives in the May prospectus management table include Ryan Carrithers (CFO), Leslie Ravestein (CLO), and Mark Brunner (CRO). The company site also lists Timothy Burns (CTO), Krishnan Anand (Chief Program Officer), and others. Board named 16 Apr 2026: Michael Blitzer (Lead Independent Director), Kenneth Braithwaite, Dr. Robert H. Smith, Kelyn Brannon (audit chair), Michael Montelongo, and Carolyn Trabuco (compensation chair). Curated director backgrounds and how they help Merlin are on the homepage Leadership and board section. (May 13 prospectus · Board PR 16 Apr 2026 · company page)
